location.name: Munich
location.institution: Deutsches Museum (replica; the original is in the Cave of Altamira)

object.medium: Replica of a painted limestone cave ceiling: ochre and charcoal on rock, reproduced in relief
object.description: The great ceiling of Altamira, where a herd of bison is painted in red ochre and outlined in black over the natural bulges of the rock, so that each animal stands out as if in relief. Found in 1879 by Marcelino Sanz de Sautuola and his young daughter María, it was the first Palaeolithic cave art recognised as such. The cave is closed to protect the paintings; this is a scan of the full-size replica in the Deutsches Museum in Munich, hung overhead as the original is, so look up.
facts: The painters used the bulges of the ceiling for the bodies of the bison, so the animals stand out in relief in raking light.
Sautuola's claim that the paintings were prehistoric was dismissed as a forgery; he died in 1888, fourteen years before the experts conceded he was right.
The ceiling is about 18 by 9 metres; the Deutsches Museum's replica was made in 1962 and is itself now a historic object.
